Description: Bronze prutahs of Herod Archelaus, ethnarch of Judaea, Samaria, and Idumaea (4 BC-AD 6), struck at the Jerusalem mint. Types include a double cornucopia with grapes paired with a war galley showing aphlaston, oars, and ram; grapes paired with a crested helmet; and an anchor paired with a wreath inscribed EΘN (Ethnarch). Inscriptions in Greek read 'of Herod' and 'of the Ethnarch'; there are no portraits, in deference to Jewish sensitivities. The galley type recalls his voyage to Rome to appeal for his father's kingdom after Herod's will was changed.
Interpretations: The coins name Herod the Ethnarch, the ruler Matthew 2:22 says Joseph feared on returning from Egypt. The galley's allusion to the Rome voyage is a scholarly reading of the imagery, not an inscriptional statement.
BiblicalSignificance: When Joseph heard that Archelaus reigned in Judaea in place of his father Herod, 'he was afraid to go thither' (Matthew 2:22) and turned aside into Galilee; these coins name the ethnarch whose reign prompted that fear.
